messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: sustained GPU queue growth in us-west-2-gpu-pool-3. Pending requests ~9k, avg queue wait 18s, autoscaler failed to add nodes (reached max_nodes=12). PagerDuty: @ashley, @omar
ashley: I'm up. hitting the logs now. any customer-facing pages?
omar: CS pinged — 3 customers seeing timeouts and higher latency. CS ticket #CS-1829.
li: quick glance at node allocation: heavy fragmentation. lots of MIG slices at 1g/2g left unused, too many pods requesting 4g. Binpacking score low.
ashley: autoscaler logs show repeated failures: "scale up requested -> denied: cluster quota or provider throttle". sending tail: 
```
2026-03-14T02:12:35Z autoscaler: RequestScaleNodes desired=20 current=12 max=12 reason=provider_limit
2026-03-14T02:12:36Z infra: AWS API rate limit 429 for DescribeInstances
2026-03-14T02:12:41Z scheduler: pending pods backoff=1m
```
omar: we hit both provider rate limits and our configured max_nodes. two problems in parallel.
ops-oncall: taking handoff for next 30m. ashley — can you summarize customer impact and an immediate mitigation plan?
ashley: summary for CS team: impact window ~02:10-02:40 UTC, 3 paying customers saw 5-10% request failures and degraded throughput; temporary mitigation: throttle non-prod and spikey endpoints, enable degraded-mode routing to smaller models if possible. CS-1829 updated.
li: reproducible cause: MIG sizing mismatch. Recent deploy introduced pods with resource request pattern that doesn't fit our common MIG configs. Many 4g requests prevent tight packing. Suggest emergency repack to merge small slices and create more 4g-capable slots.
nate: I can run an emergency binpack and soft-evict low-priority pods. Plan: 1) mark pool 'eviction-ok', 2) run packer to co-locate 4g pods, 3) scale up smaller nodes if needed.
ashley: warning — evictions will affect background jobs and some free-tier customers. need CS signoff for evicting non-paying queues. @cs-sara thoughts?
cs-sara: ok to evict background and free-tier batch jobs for up to 10 min, keep premium customers untouched. go ahead.
omar: executing step 1. running command: 
```
./rebalancer --pool us-west-2-gpu-pool-3 --mode emergency --target-requests-per-node 1200 --evict-priority low --dry-run=false
```
li: also patching scheduler policy to prefer 4g slices for newly scheduled pods while repack is ongoing. applying policy change now.
incident-bot: Manual intervention recorded by ashley at 02:22 UTC: emergency-repack started.
omar: autoscaler still hitting provider throttle. two parallel mitigations: (A) repack to free capacity for 4g pods, (B) request temporary raise with cloud provider/activate reserved burst capacity. I've opened ticket with provider ops ticket #AWS-8891 and requested burst pool activation. ETA unknown.
nate: repack completed step A: reclaimed ~8 GPUs worth of usable 4g slots by consolidating 1g/2g slices. immediate drop in queue ~40%.
ashley: monitoring customer errors — failure rate dropped to 1.2% from 6.8%. still elevated latency ~+25% for a subset of requests.
ops-oncall: marking this incident as partial mitigation. continuing monitoring and follow-up actions: 1) provider quota check, 2) autoscaler config: bump max_nodes to 24 for emergency window, 3) longer-term: review MIG templates and implement automatic slice reshaping on deploy.
omar: bumping max_nodes requires approval and quota from billing. starting emergency approval flow now.
pagerduty-bot: @ops-oncall acknowledged. escalation to infra-leads if degradation persists for >30m.
li: note for postmortem — root cause chain: new pod request mix + MIG template drift after recent runtime change + autoscaler conservative max_nodes + provider API throttling => stranded capacity despite available physical GPUs.
ashley: postmortem actions (short): 1) implement pre-deploy MIG-resize check, 2) autoscaler to attempt speculative repack before scaling, 3) temporary policy: protect premium customers by draining non-critical work first.
cs-sara: CS will reach out to affected customers with a summary and goodwill credits.
ops-oncall: handing back to oncall rotation, leaving runbook steps in thread. I'll stay reachable in case provider burst takes too long.
ashley: closing incident once error rates are back to baseline and queues stable for 20m. current metrics: pending queue 2.1k -> trending down, error rate 0.9%, avg latency +12%.
incident-bot: Incident status updated to "mitigated (partial)" at 02:48 UTC. Follow-up: schedule postmortem and assign action items.
ashley: assigning postmortem owner: li. li: will run RCA and schedule with infra and runtime teams.
li: acknowledged. starting notes now; will include replay of repack commands and scheduling changes.
